title: The occult philosopher
summary: An intellectual lettrist, Akhlāṭī's disciple and systematizer, whose Mafāḥiṣ (completed 823/1420) aims at a universal science of the letter, whose confession is imamophile Shiʿi-Sunnism, and whose apologies are what he told his judges. The model is Melvin-Koushki's thesis, and it carries his own concessions: a rearranger and popularizer, 'an apostle of Akhlāṭī'; the Tamhīd 'certainly not minor'; the study provisional.
